literal: While tender thorn-tree let one destroy; of those who weed out hand it will hurt hardened at the time.
translation: Cut down a thorny tree while it is still young and tender. If you wait until its trunk has hardened, it will injure the hands of those who try to chop it.
modern: முள்மரத்தை அது இளமையாக இருக்கும்போதே வெட்டிவிட வேண்டும். அது முதிர்ந்து வயிரம் பாய்ந்த பிறகு வெட்ட நினைத்தால், வெட்டுபவரின் கையையே அது காயப்படுத்தும்.
explanation: This couplet uses the vivid metaphor of a thorny tree to explain how to handle enemies. A thorny sapling is easy to uproot, but a mature one will injure the person trying to cut it down. Similarly, a foe's power should be dismantled while it is still weak and developing. If left to grow strong and entrenched, the enemy will cause great harm to anyone who attempts to defeat them later.
